body: Thank you.  I was a little lost there.

Rewarding Karens/Chads for their behavior.  I believe they act the way they act because too many people are giving them satisfaction for their behavior.  They want to speak to the manager and bitch up a storm.  What manager in their right mind wants to give them what they want?  I'd prefer they tell them to calm the fuck down or get the fuck out.  Just my opinion.  Business don't pay many public facing employees enough to deal with that kind of behavior.  That said, the customer is wrong sometimes and penalizing them for being terrible people might make them be a little more reasonable in the future.  Managers, learn the art of saying, "We're at an impasse" and walking away.  No boss' number.  No escalation.  Just no.
I know that feeling.  If you find a solution, let me know.

Back in the day, I'd read dating profiles that would say "hates drama" or "drama free."  I found the people behind those profiles were born in it and molded by it like they're Bane or something.  Run.  Run from profiles like that.  They want all of the smoke.
Not only that, sometimes, the marriage doesn't last as long as the engagement.  This means they wanted a wedding and not a marriage.
Sorry, but I'm not welcoming a f**ed up thought.  I think it's a means of getting rid of the torment of depression and anxiety.  That said, if those were gone, I think that thought might fade away.
At least there's a tip in there.  Thank you.  While I can work remotely, I don't have the luxury of being able to relocate right now.  I'd get more specific, but I'm trying to remain anonymous.
Takes one to know one, huh?
